claims.text: Chemical short-range order can form in a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy such as HfNbTaTiZr.
Controlled annealing at 1000–1500 K will promote the evolution and eventual percolation of SRO clusters.
SRO is thermodynamically stable above 0.5 Tm while the alloy remains single-phase bcc and avoids intermetallic ordering.
Percolating SRO clusters form a connected network of extended phonon-scattering centers.
Percolating SRO will produce a non-linear reduction in thermal conductivity that exceeds serial, parallel, or effective-medium mixing-model predictions.
The SRO percolation threshold will occur at a volume fraction of approximately 0.3–0.4.
Simple point-defect scattering scales linearly with SRO concentration.
SRO clusters in the bcc alloy generate local strain fields and mass-difference fluctuations.
Isolated SRO clusters scatter phonons through Rayleigh scattering with cross-section proportional to the fourth power of phonon frequency.
Once SRO clusters percolate, phonon mean free path becomes limited by cluster spacing rather than individual-defect size.
The connected SRO network creates a phonon-glass-like state and causes a super-linear reduction in thermal conductivity.
Standard mixing models fail because they assume independent scattering events and omit collective scattering by a percolating SRO network.
The potential-energy surface must contain strong local minima for particular atomic pairings, such as Hf-Ta or Nb-Zr, to stabilize the proposed SRO clusters.
Standard empirical interatomic potentials often fail to capture the local energetic features needed to predict SRO evolution.
Highly accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials can be used in molecular-dynamics studies of SRO effects in bcc refractory high-entropy alloys.
Thermal conductivity will drop by more than 20% from the disordered baseline when the SRO network reaches its percolation threshold.
The SRO-containing alloy will have lower thermal conductivity than a random solid solution with equivalent average scattering strength.
The percolation mechanism applies only if SRO clusters connect without producing B2 ordering, bcc decomposition, an intermetallic, or a second phase.
The exact percolation threshold and conductivity reduction depend on pair-interaction energies in HfNbTaTiZr.
A broad SRO cluster-size distribution may turn the proposed sharp transition into a gradual conductivity change.
